 Ben Duckett and Sam Curran in action running between the wickets. Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/Reuters View image in fullscreen Ben Duckett and Sam Curran in action running between the wickets. Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/Reuters Daniel Gallan Sun 25 Oct 2026 06.32 EDT First published on Sun 25 Oct 2026 03.09 EDT Share Key events 23m ago WICKET! Curran c Salman b Shaheen 42 (England

 2h ago WICKET! Brook run-out Razuallah 1 (England 19-3)

 now 06.32 EDT Dean Kinsella has written in: 
 double quotation mark Good morning (afternoon?) Daniel. I’m all over the place with the time change. Nearly missed my bus from Faro to Lisbao, then had an hour to kill as I was an hour early. 
 Anyhow, as a result, I missed the start. Was it a new ball(s) thing? Lots of swing etc? Doesn’t look too bad of a strip right now 
 Combo of poor batting – or rather, meek batting – some good catching and lovely zip off the surface for the new ball. But Banton, Root and Brook pretty much gave their wickets away.
 Share 1m ago 06.30 EDT 31st over: England 165-5 (Duckett 93, Jacks 9) Arafat continues, looking to bag the big wicket of Duckett who doesn’t love facing left arm finger spinners. Both batters rotate well, collecting six runs off the over by working the gaps and staying patient.
 Share 4m ago 06.27 EDT 30th over: England 159-5 (Duckett 91, Jacks 5) Duckett moves into the 90s with a tickle to Rauf’s opening ball that skips away fine for four. Jacks, who was quietly brilliant against Sri Lanka with 66 not-out off 33 balls, gets to work here with a couple off his pads before a single through the covers.
 Share 13m ago 06.19 EDT 29th over: England 151-5 (Duckett 86, Jacks 2) Finally we have Arafat, who bagged six English wickets a few days ago. He’s starting well, getting some skid off the pitch. He almost beats Duckett, who is back to a ball he should have pressed forward to. Duckett looks uncomfortable off a small sample size of five dot balls in a row. Duckett manages to plink a single down the ground, but that’s a good start from the left arm spinner, conceding just one run off that set.
 Share 15m ago 06.16 EDT 28th over: England 150-5 (Duckett 85, Jacks 2) Shadab convinces Shaheen to review but it’s a wasted one. Encouraging signs though as he got that to grip and turn sharply back into Duckett’s pad. But it was turning too much to bother the stumps. Jacks rotates and picks up a couple of singles. Duckett sweeps well, but he picks out the fielder between fine leg and deep square, so settles for just one to bring up the 150.
 Share 19m ago 06.13 EDT Shadab is convinced that Duckett is plumb lbw! He insists on reviewing the not-out decision. Looked like it was angling to me. Yup, that was turning sharply and down leg.
 Share 21m ago 06.11 EDT 27th over: England 145-5 (Duckett 83, Jacks 0) Well then, after all that hard graft from Curran he’s gone. Pretty poor if you ask me. He neither took on the bouncer nor looked to rude the bounce. Just a tame waft at the lifting ball and it was a comfortable catch just off the rope. pakistan’s captain strikes in an over worth just two runs. Duckett needs to carry his bat (which I’m sure he’s trying to do anyway).
 Share 23m ago 06.08 EDT WICKET! Curran c Salman b Shaheen 42 (England
 A bolt from the blue! Totally against the run of play, Curran takes on Shaheen’s bouncer but can only catch it with the top edge. It sails in an arc towards the fielder down at fine leg who runs in off the rope to take the comfortable catch. Credit to the bowler for digging it in, but that is tame from Curran who has thrown away a golden opportunity here.
 Share 27m ago 06.05 EDT 26th over: England 143-4 (Duckett 82, Curran 41) Duckett is in full flow now. Over pitched from Shadab, but he plays this perfectly, clearing his front leg as he drives wide of mid-off while presenting the full face of the bat to pick up four runs. That’s the shot of the day for me. Then it’s a case of rotating the strike as the partnership reaches 91.
 Share 30m ago 06.01 EDT 25th over: England 135-4 (Duckett 75, Curran 40) Shaheen recognises that something has to change so he’s back on to do it himself. His first ball is a rank half-tracker that Duckett spanks for four through midwicket. After the madness at the top, both batters now look totally in control.
 Share 34m ago 05.57 EDT 24th over: England 128-4 (Duckett 69, Curran 39) Not sure what Shaheen is waiting for before bringing on his primary strike spin bowler. But there’s still no Arafat. Shadab bowls some darts and coughs up three singles, so its not exactly a disaster, but he doesn’t look like getting a wicket. Pakistan need to break this partnership. It feels like they’re letting England drift a little.
 Share 38m ago 05.53 EDT 23rd over: England 125-4 (Duckett 67, Curran 38) Duckett nails a sweep shot off Salman. He never bothered keeping it down and gets a whole lot of it as it sails over midwicket for six. He barely touched it and het it exploded off the willow. Then he reverses and lofts it over the man at short third. Wonderful batting, toying with the bowler. He then collects a single off the last ball to keep the strike before needing some minor medical attention. Not sure what the issue is as he has a chat with the physio, but he’ll be OK I’m sure.
 Share 41m ago 05.50 EDT 22nd over: England 113-4 (Duckett 56, Curran 37) Oooh, Duckett gets low to play a premeditated scoop. He gets one for it but he barely got down in time. Had he missed he’d be lbw for sure! Still no Arafat, who bagged a six-for last time out against England.
 Share 45m ago 05.47 EDT 21st over: England 108-4 (Duckett 53, Curran 35) Duckett brings up his 50 with a bunt down the ground. He’s helped dig his team out of a deep hole here but has plenty of work left to do. Curran adds another single with a cut down to deep point before Duckett sweeps for two and then drives down the ground for one. They’re rotating the strike well. Curran keeps the strike with another single off the last ball.
 Share 47m ago 05.44 EDT 20th over: England 102-4 (Duckett 49, Curran 33) Leg spin now as Shadab Khan finally enters from stage right. He’s not looping or ripping it, but the change of angle and direction of turn at least gives the batters something else to consider. Ducket brings up the 50-run stand with a reverse sweep down to the fielder at deep backward point.
 Share 52m ago 05.39 EDT 19th over: England 98-4 (Duckett 48, Curran 30) Salman isn’t exactly threatening, but he’s keeping things tidy. Is that enough for Shaheen after the blistering start for Pakistan? Both batters look comfortable knocking about singles as their partnership reaches 45.
 Share Updated at  05.42 EDT 55m ago 05.36 EDT 18th over: England 95-5 (Duckett 47, Curran 29) Curran rocks back and nails a pull shot to Razaullah’s half-tracker for four, getting it well in front of square. Rather than correct his length and go fuller, he drops it even shorter, giving away a wide over Duckett’s head. That’s the exuberance of youth – he is only 21. When he shows more control, hitting a good length, he looks more menacing.
 Share Updated at  05.37 EDT 1h ago 05.32 EDT 17th over: England 89-4 (Duckett 47, Curran 23) We’re fully in the middle overs period of this ODI now. Good from Salman, just the right pace and flight and drift to keep the batters honest. Three singles across the set. Pakistan won’t mind that.
 Share 1h ago 05.29 EDT 16th over: England 86-4 (Duckett 46, Curran 21) Razaullah returns and is steaming in, banging away at a good length, angling it into the left-handers as he attempts to cramp them up. He does well, keeping Curran to just one single and Duckett scoreless.
 Really interested to see how Curran goes now. This is a perfect opportunity to dig in and register a score that secures his place in the team for an extended run. What an opportunity for him.
 Share 1h ago 05.25 EDT 15th over: England 85-4 (Duckett 46, Curran 20) Salman on and he’s immediately tidier than Saim who was missing his length on the shorter side. Salman is tossing it up and inviting the England batters to press forward. Just the three singles from that set.
 Share 1h ago 05.21 EDT 14th over: England 82-4 (Duckett 44, Curran 19) Rauf cuts Duckett in half with one that jags back in on the angle from a good length. A whisker away from both the inside edge and the top of off. Duckett is up for the challenge, though, as he smokes one through midwicket for four. That came down at 89mph but must have left the bat at twice that speed from rolled wrists in front of square.
 Share 1h ago 05.14 EDT 13th over: England 78-4 (Duckett 40, Curran 19) Time for a drink as England’s batters get a chance to gather themselves for the next shift. This over from Saim is closed off with a four for Curran who leans back and cracks a half cut, half punch well in front of square and finds a big gap at deep extra cover. Saim has now bowled two drag downs in each of his overs and has been punished.
 Share 1h ago 05.10 EDT 12th over: England 71-4 (Duckett 38, Curran 14) Rauf continues and there’s the first mistake from Pakistan as the fielder at backward point makes a mess of a routine stop, allowing Curran to gather one. Otherwise it’s a tidy set from the right-armer who is round the wicket into the left-handed batters. Duckett keeps the strike with a tickle down to fine leg.
 Here’s what reader Guy Hornsby makes of it all:
 double quotation mark Well this is a good one to get up for, Daniel! Root and Banton out hitting it out of the middle of the bat but Brook’s second was never on, and Cox just seemed to gently guide it to slip. I guess Sam Curran won’t have a better chance to redeem himself after the Sri Lanka game than now. It feels we’re into the ‘just go harder’ phase of the game. This could be 280 or 140 all out. Amazing how good Pakistan are with all their quicks... If only they were allowed play in the Test team! 
 Share 1h ago 05.04 EDT 11th over: England 67-4 (Duckett 36, Curran 13) Spin now as Saim joins the party. What a perfect time for the spinner to come on. His seamers have provided the perfect platform but the English batters won’t want to let him settle. Curran spots that mid-on is up and heaves one up and over him for four. He didn’t get all of it, but there was enough welly on it. Saim over corrects and drags down a long-hop that Curran smears off the back foot through cow corner for another four. Curran, who is only batting in the powerplay of an ODI for the third time in his career, bunts a single to get off steike before Duckett caresses one of his own to the sweeper on the off side. Productive from the English.
 Share 2h ago 05.00 EDT 10th over: England 56-4 (Duckett 34, Curran 4) That’s the end of the powerplay and it’s fair to say Pakistan have bossed it. Another tame wicket though, so England haven’t exactly helped themselves. What was Cox thinking there? Anyway, Curran looks good so far. One firm cut is well fielded before he climbs into a short ball and pulls it well for four on the leg side. Duckett the lone ranger right now. Pakistan have bowled and fielded well, no doubt, but England have been the architects of their own doom.
 Share 2h ago 04.54 EDT WICKET! Cox c Babar b Rauf Cox 6 (England 52-4)
 Easy as you like! That was literally catching practice for Babar Azam at slip. I mean literally. You know how fielding coaches will offer catching practice for their players before the start of play? That. Back of a length, too close to cut but with enough bounce that the steer from an angled bat was always going to be tricky, Cox meekly prods at it and says to Babar, ‘catch that if you can’. You bet he can, getting both hands to one around shoulder height to his right. England in a serious pickle now!
 Share 2h ago 04.52 EDT 9th over: England 52-3 (Duckett 34, Cox 6) Shaheen continues and offers just a smidge of width to Duckett who needs no second invite to throw his hands at it. He doesn’t find the middle of the bat but there’s enough wood on the edge to see it fly down to deep third for four. Afridi then unfurls a slower ball but Duckett is wise to it as he steers a single behind square. Cox collects a single as well, dabbing one past the slip fielder to deep third.
 Share 2h ago 04.47 EDT Reader David Williams is not enjoying what he’s seeing: 
 double quotation mark Wonder which bowlers get dropped as an excuse this time. Should have stayed in bed despite the extra hour rather than watching this shambles. 
 Hope you treat yourself to a tasty breakfast to lighten your mood.
 Share 2h ago 04.46 EDT 8th over: England 46-3 (Duckett 29, Cox 5) Change of bowling as Rauf comes into the attack. He’s wicket to wicket to Cox who has to be watchful. Cox opens his account with a firm punch back down the ground which beats the diving Shaheen and mid-on and skips away to the rope. Lovely balance there. He’s back up the other end with a steer to deep third which brings Duckett on strike who squirts a full ball off the inside half of his bat down to fine leg worth three. Better running from the England batters.
 Share 2h ago 04.41 EDT 7th over: England 38-3 (Duckett 26, Cox 0) Shaheen is finding extra lift off the surface. Duckett has to be watchful as he looks down on the surface as if its made of spitting snakes. But when he gets a juicy ball on his pads, Duckett flicks his wrists and collects four runs through square leg. The next ball is a drag down and Duckett swivels as he pulls with aplomb, rolling his wrists as he collects four more.
 Share 2h ago 04.37 EDT 6th over: England 30-3 (Duckett 18, Cox 0) Just for a second Duckett’s heart was in his mouth as he hoiked a short ball from Razaullah down to fine leg. If the fielder was on the rope, as he should have been, it would have been a simple catch. Instead it sailed over his head for six. The bowler sends a death stare down to his mate. His mood sours as Duckett punches the next ball for four backward of point and then he scampers up the other end with a single. That brings new man Cox on strike who is watchful across an over worth 11 runs.
 Share 2h ago 04.34 EDT Replays show that Brook slipped as he turned at the non-striker’s end. Without it he might have made his ground. Still, that never looked like two to me.
 Share 2h ago 04.31 EDT WICKET! Brook run-out Razuallah 1 (England 19-3)
 The England captain has just run himself out! Why on earth did he come back for a second? A thick inside edge off Shaheen had the ball squirt down to fine leg, but it was pretty much straight to the debutant who got his throw away quickly after a swift one-handed pick-up. Brook ran the first one hard and then called Duckett back for the second. He was running towards the danger end but that was self destructive! If the throw and pick-up from the keeper were clean, as they both were, he was never making his ground. England in real trouble now.
 5th over: England 19-3 (Duckett 7) 
 View image in fullscreen Pakistan's Saad Baig reacts after Harry Brook loses his wicket, run out by Razaullah. Photograph: Akhtar Soomro/Reuters Share Updated at  06.15 EDT 2h ago 04.25 EDT 4th over: England 18-1 (Duckett 7, Brook 0) Good wheels from Razaullah who beats Ducket with genuine pace. But Duckett won’t go in his shell and throws his hands at some width as he gets it up and over the infield on the off side. Duckett then shows a bit more control as he pings a drive on the up in front of cover and adds two runs to his score.
 Share 2h ago 04.20 EDT 3rd over: England 11-2 (Duckett 1, Brook 0) This couldn’t be going better as far as Pakistan are concerned. Shaheen’s angle across the right-hander has done for Banton and now Root, who timed his cut shot well but couldn’t find a gap either side of Saim at backward point. Brook, the new man, lets an in-swinger go that wans’t too far away from nipping back onto his off stump. The skipper has a big job to do here.
 Share 2h ago 04.17 EDT WICKET! Root c Saim b Shaheen 5 (England 11-2)
 Loose from Root! Oh my, that’s two in two for the Pakistan skipper. This was short and wide and begging to be hit. Root obliged but he thwacked it straight at Saim at backward point who made a sharp catch low down look routine. The ball before Root had flicked Shaheen through square leg for four but falls this time, admonishing himself as he leaves the scene. What a start for Pakistan!
 Share 2h ago 04.12 EDT 2nd over: England 6-1 (Duckett 1, Root 1) Razaullah on ODI debut opens up from the other end. Right arm, bustling to the crease, quick arms whirring in a chaotic, slingy action, he’s seems plucked from central casting and I’m here for it! He finds a thick edge of Duckett’s wayward drive, but it flies down to deep third for one. Root gets off the mark before Duckett looks to carve a shorter ball over the infield, but hits nothing but air.
 Share 2h ago 04.08 EDT 1st over: England 4-1 (Duckett 0, Root 0) What a start for Pakistan. Shaheen was looking for swing and went full for most of the over, but it was the one just a touch shorter that saw to Banton as he went looking for a booming drive on the up. Root, in much earlier than he’d have liked, gets a full in-swinger than thwacks his pads, but it was always going down leg. Top work from the home team.
 Share 2h ago 04.05 EDT WICKET! Banton c Arafat b Shaheen 4 (England 4-1)
 A wicket in the first over! It’s a tame dismissal. Having whipped a half volley for four through mdwicket two balls earlier, Banton was looking to drive through cover. But it stands up in the pitch just a touch and wasn’t quite full enough to simply throw his hands at it. In the end he scoops a simple catch to Arafat at short extra cover. Pakistan up and running thanks to their skipper’s 150th scalp in this format.
 Share 3h ago 04.01 EDT It will be the captain, Shaheen Afridi, all 6’ 6” of him, who will open up. 
 Banton will face the first ball.
 Share 3h ago 03.59 EDT The Pakistan players, in bright pink, are gathered on the side of the field, engaged in a team talk and ready to let rip at England. 
 England’s openers, in blue different hues of blue, have bumped fists and are making their way to the middle. Can they get their team off to a decent start this time?
 Share 3h ago 03.50 EDT Mark Butcher is touching the surface now. 
 Looks a road. But what do I know? The last time England played here they failed to defend 352 against Australia.
 Runs, runs and more runs is what I foresee on a fast and true deck.
 Share 3h ago 03.49 EDT Chris Woakes is on my screen speaking like a veteran pundit. 
 Good opportunity to share this from his co-author, our very own Ali Martin:
 The Spin | Writing a book with Chris Woakes showed the inner steel of the nicest man in cricket Read more Share 3h ago 03.40 EDT Pakistan team
 Two changes from their last game. 
 Pace bowler Razaullah makes his debut and Shadab Kahan returns to the side. Naseem Shah dislocated his finger in the warm up, though his skipper says he’ll be fine for the next match. Faheem Ashraf misses out today as well.
 Pakistan: Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam, Saad Baig (wk), Salman Alo Agha, Hasan Nawaz, Arafat Minhas, Shadab Khan, Shaheen Shah Afridi (c), Razaullah, Haris Rauf.
 Share 3h ago 03.39 EDT England team
 A bowler was always going to get the axe and its Josh Tongue who misses out. 
 In comes Henry Crocombe to make his debut. Inexplicably, Adil Rashid continues to warm the bench.
 England: Tom Banton, Ben Duckett, Joe Root, Harry Brook (c), Jordon Cox (wk), Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Liam Dawson, Gus Atkinson, Henry Crocombe.
 Share Updated at  03.39 EDT 3h ago 03.33 EDT Pakistan win the toss and bowl
 Shaheen Afridi gets the coin flip go his way and wants to bowl. 
 He cites the ‘fresh’ surface as a reason for his decision, wanting to get a look at it before having a bat.
 Share 3h ago 03.31 EDT Anyone else seeing a red glass on the bottom right corner of their screen? 
 I promise I’m not at a pub!
 Anyway, here comes the toss…
 Share 3h ago 03.26 EDT There’s been a late call up for Maaz Sadaqat to the Pakistan squad. He replaces the injured left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqeem.
 Oh, worth also mentioning that Pakistan will wear pink today, taking a lead out of South Africa’s book as they change from their natural green to raise funds and awarness for breast cancer.
 Share 3h ago 03.18 EDT Reports are it’s nice and sunny in Lahore. Should be a belter of a day. Expect loads of runs.
 Share 3h ago 03.13 EDT While you settle in, why not catch up on some reading (Barney’s piece on Temba Bavuma is quite excellent)": 
 Bavuma’s nine-hour masterpiece was art we risk losing in Test cricket’s great purge | Barney Ronay Read more Winds of change are coming for Australia as selection storm brews in South Africa | Martin Pegan Read more Sri Lanka stun England with second-highest ODI chase despite Brook’s 202 Read more Share 3h ago 03.09 EDT Preamble
 Daniel Gallan For the past two days, I’ve not been able to get Harry Brook out of my mind. 
 What has been going through his head since he clobbered and caressed his way to the fastest double-century in ODI history, a staggering 202 from 116 balls, only to watch his bowlers fail to defend 430 ?
 What’s the equivalent in another sport? Scoring six goals in football only for your defence to concede seven in the second half? Hitting every fairway in golf, then four-putting every green?
 Brook is back in action as England face Pakistan for the second time in this tri-series. Pakistan won the teams’ previous meeting by 87 runs , with Brook making five as England’s batters folded against Arafat Minhas’ six-for; bowled out for 215.
 A win would send Pakistan into the final with a game to spare, and they have the chance to do it at their Lahore HQ. For England, a third straight defeat in this format, less than a year before the World Cup, would deepen the questions. They need to put together a complete performance.
 Will they do it? We’ll find out when things get going at 8am UK time.
 Got your coffee and toast? Let’s get stuck in!
